I'd like to get that check scheduled and hear from each of those areas so we can move forward. Could representatives from those four areas please share their current readiness status regarding the bariatric lift?

transcript.text: I'd like to share my physical therapy assessment findings for both patients. The South unit patient failed the sit-to-stand assessment and requires a full-body bariatric lift for every bed-to-chair transfer. The North unit patient can currently complete a two-person stand-pivot transfer with a gait belt. Based on clinical need, the South unit patient has the more urgent requirement for the bariatric lift.

transcript.text: I need to share an important facilities finding regarding the lift. The available lift is the Titan-MB model, which has a 48-inch turning radius. This fits South room 412's 50-inch doorway, but North room 318 has a 36-inch doorway and cannot safely accommodate this lift. Additionally, the charger must be placed in the South 4B equipment alcove. From a facilities standpoint, the lift can only be safely used on the South unit.

transcript.text: From a nursing education standpoint, I can confirm that three South-unit nurses have completed the lift competency validation. Hospital policy requires two validated staff members for every lift transfer, and South unit's validated staff coverage is available from 07:00 to 19:00 daily. This means South can meet the staffing requirement for safe lift transfers during those hours.

These infection control measures need to be built into the operational plan before the lift assignment is finalized.
